answer: Agents could require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit an order, then slash that stake when an order is proven to violate the market’s rules. Splitting one agent into many accounts does not multiply influence for free: each account needs its own capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing it. The river of accounts may look wide, but a sonnet of fake names still pays for every voice; one detected scheme sends a costly ripple through the attacker’s stake.
